Study of remains taken from royal cemetery at Umm el-Qa’ab appears to confirm early Egyptologist’s theory

Court officials and craftspeople serving early Egyptian kings may have been sacrificed when their ruler died, according to research that found fractures in several ancient skulls.

The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC.

guardian.description:
Progressive voters and supporters of incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva left reeling after far-right surge

Voters in Quebec are going to the polls in provincial elections which will probably result in victory for a party that has promised to hold a referendum on independence from Canada within the next two years.

A US marine stationed on Japan’s southern island of Okinawa is accused of murdering a Japanese woman and has been arrested on suspicion of murder, police said on Sunday.

Britain under pressure to put tariffs on cheap Chinese vehicle imports ahead of protectionist trade measures

Britain’s car industry is grappling with a “difficult trade-off” between China and Europe, as manufacturers struggle to balance the benefits of both markets ahead of looming trade measures that could restrict UK exports to the EU.

rfi.title: French MEP Hassan under investigation over flag incident at 7 October commemoration
rfi.description: Hard-left French EU lawmaker Rima Hassan is facing an investigation after the Israeli and European Union flags were allegedly thrown to the floor at a commemoration for the 2023 Hamas attacks that set off the Gaza war. Hassan said the action was to denounce the "ongoing genocide by the Israeli government".

rfi.title: EU suspends beef exports from Namibia due to foot and mouth disease
rfi.description: The largest market for Namibian beef, the European Union, announced it has suspended imports after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, which wreaked havoc in Europe 25 years ago.

rfi.title: France earmarks a further €7m to help fight DRC's worst-ever Ebola crisis
rfi.description: France has decided to allocate an additional €7 million this year to combat the Ebola epidemic currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This comes as Kenya announced its first-ever death from the disease.

rfi.title: Quebec separatist party wins provincial election in test of Canada's unity
rfi.description: Separatists won provincial elections in Quebec on Monday, with a promise to hold a vote on leaving Canada after US President Donald Trump leaves office, testing Prime Minister Mark Carney's message of national unity.

rfi.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
rfi.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

rfi.title: Olise strikes twice in France's romp past Belgium in Nations League
rfi.description: Désiré Doué, Ryan Cherki and two goals from Michael Olise launched the late pyrotechnics on Monday night at the Stade de France as France scored four times in 13 minutes to whoosh past Belgium 4-1 and maintain the lead of their Nations League pool.

rfi.title: Lebanon joined by UK and France for three weeks of joint military drills
rfi.description: Lebanon's army will hold three weeks of exercises with the British military from Tuesday, both sides said on Monday, with the drills to involve personnel and representatives from countries including France, Italy and the United States.

rfi.title: Climate change driving child marriages and teen pregnancies, study finds
rfi.description: The charity Plan International said on Monday that global warming has increased the risk of child marriages, teenage pregnancies and violence against girls. Its report coincides with talks in the South Pacific nations of Fiji and Tuvalu, where climate change is affecting all aspects of daily life.

rfi.title: Study shows extreme poverty and homelessness on the rise in France
rfi.description: An international study published on Monday by France’s largest food aid charity, Restos du Cœur, shows the number of people living in extreme poverty in France and other wealthy countries increased by 37 percent between 2018 and 2025.

rfi.title: Chat group kingpin goes on trial in Paris over online abuse of underage girls
rfi.description: A 29-year-old man went on trial on Monday at the Paris Assize Court, charged with running a masculinist chat group on the platform Discord on which young victims were forced to engage in sexual acts online and to mutilate themselves.

rfi.title: Spain PM calls early election after housing crisis defeat
rfi.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday called a snap election for 29 November, after parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government. This comes after tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities on Saturday to demand affordable housing.

rfi.title: US-German trio win medicine Nobel for work on optogenetics
rfi.description: The Nobel medicine prize was awarded Monday to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their work in the field of optogenetics.

rfi.title: Nobel Prize announcements begin, with hopes of a 'less controversial year'
rfi.description: With this year's Nobel Prize winner announcements beginning on Monday, among those experts believe could be in line for the $1.2 million prizes are GLP-1 researchers, a Ukrainian children's rights activist and several female authors. And after last year's Donald Trump-driven controversy, anticipation around this year's Peace Prize is high.

rfi.title: The pill: from symbol of women's liberation to subject of growing mistrust
rfi.description: Initially a symbol of liberation, the pill went on to become an almost inevitable part of a woman’s contraceptive journey. But today its use in France is in decline, the drop in popularity fuelled by health warnings, mistrust and a changing attitude towards contraception.

rfi.title: Ethiopia captures Tigray capital as its regional rivals meet in Egypt
rfi.description: Ethiopian federal forces have regained control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, local sources said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

rfi.title: France struggles to fund farm climate adaptation as losses mount
rfi.description: Farmers in France are expecting their first payments shortly under the government's billion-euro emergency aid package to support farmers affected by severe summer heatwaves, droughts and wildfires. As the effects of climate change worsen, experts say compensation alone will not be enough to protect French agriculture in the long term.

rfi.title: Rwandan genocide hunter Dafroza Gauthier dies after long battle for justice
rfi.description: Dafroza Gauthier, who spent spent decades tracking down Rwandans in France accused of involvement in the 1994 genocide, has died from cancer at the age of 72. By filing a string of civil lawsuits against suspected fugitives, she and her husband Alain pushed the French legal system to hold them to account.

rfi.title: Reintroduction of vultures to France causes friction with farmers
rfi.description: France’s vulture population is growing, thanks to a reintroduction campaign that began in the 1980s after the birds all but disappeared decades earlier. But according to some farmers, the return of the birds has brought challenges as well as rewards.

euronews.title: One student killed, eight wounded in Istanbul school stabbing attack
euronews.description: A 15-year-old student disguised herself in the target school's uniform before attacking pupils at Şeyh Şamil Imam Hatip Secondary School in Başakşehir on Tuesday morning. The suspect, who attends a different school, was apprehended.

euronews.title: Book weighing over 200kg illustrated by Dalí and Cocteau stolen in Auvergne
euronews.description: On the night of 4 to 5 October, the "Book of the Apocalypse", a 210‑kilo volume with works by Salvador Dalí, Jean Cocteau and Bernard Buffet, was stolen from an art centre in Issoire, Puy‑de‑Dôme.

euronews.title: EU-China trade tensions: Five things to know as Brussels and Beijing face crunch talks
euronews.description: The next ten days will be critical for EU-China relations. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič will travel to Beijing later this week for high-level talks aimed at rebalancing the trade relationship and securing “tangible” results ahead of next week’s meeting of EU leaders.

euronews.title: Brussels eyes agricultural carve-outs from Ukraine's EU membership
euronews.description: The European Commission proposed excluding Ukraine's agricultural products from the EU market and agricultural funding even when Kyiv joins the EU, in a move to smooth the country's accession process and address concerns from several member states.

euronews.title: Russia denies plague death but quarantines hundreds without explanation
euronews.description: Rospotrebnadzor said Darya Shipilova, 28, died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology" with no links to her work at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, but imposed quarantine on her contacts, confined 60 colleagues inside the facility and restricted access to hospitals including a maternity ward.

euronews.title: Third day of national action by secondary school pupils and students in France
euronews.description: The protesters, joined by parents and trade unions, are condemning the lack of resources in the national education system.

euronews.title: Lithuania takes further step towards lifting nuclear weapons ban
euronews.description: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday that Lithuania’s move, alongside broader plans to expand US and NATO military infrastructure in the region, risked further escalating tensions.

euronews.title: New EU members face 15-year probation period after joining the bloc
euronews.description: The European Commission is proposing a new procedure to cut funding and voting rights of EU newcomers that breach the rule of law, available for 15 years after accession. The proposal also includes new procedures for the gradual integration of candidate countries and governance measures.

euronews.title: 'Whole world is paying' for Iran war, Qatar warns as mediation efforts continue
euronews.description: The Iran war has disrupted global trade as regional powers prepare to bolster Saudi Arabia’s defences. Qatar said talks to end the war remained active and backed the Mecca defence alliance, but added that it was too early to discuss joining the pact.

euronews.title: EU countries to discuss suspected plague outbreak in Russia
euronews.description: European health authorities are closely following the suspected plague outbreak in Siberia, Russia. The European Commission and member states are set to discuss the matter on Wednesday morning.

euronews.title: Metsola to take action after MEP Rima Hassan removes Israeli flag
euronews.description: French pro-Palestinian MEP Rima Hassan removed Israeli and EU flags from an exhibition commemorating the victims of Hamas’s 7 October terrorist attack, sparking outrage among fellow lawmakers. She could face a suspension of her daily allowance.

euronews.title: EU Commission throws down the gauntlet to member states on reforming the bloc
euronews.description: The European Commission is proposing fewer commissioners and less unanimity to prepare the EU for 30 or more members. However, EU diplomats say capitals are unlikely to agree.

euronews.title: Two Spanish F-18 jets scrambled in Romania after drone alert near Ukraine
euronews.description: Two Spanish F-18s deployed in Romania under NATO command took off at dawn after two air targets were detected near the Ukrainian border. The objects did not ultimately enter Romanian airspace and were not intercepted.

euronews.title: France test-fires new nuclear-capable missile from submarine for first time
euronews.description: "To be free, one must be feared," Emmanuel Macron has posted, weeks after vowing that hybrid attacks blamed on Russia would "not go unanswered".

euronews.title: Paramount and Warner Bros complete merger to form Hollywood giant Skydance
euronews.description: Two of America’s oldest film studios have completed their merger, bringing CNN, HBO and franchises including The Godfather and Harry Potter under one roof.

euronews.title: Burnout at work: MEPs call for stronger EU protections
euronews.description: MEPs called for EU-wide rules to tackle work-related stress, depression and anxiety, which affect almost one in three workers. Far-right groups opposed the text, arguing that it would place excessive obligations on businesses.

euronews.title: From desalination to irrigation: How countries are adapting to water scarcity
euronews.description: From desalination in the UAE to modernising irrigation systems in Uzbekistan, countries facing water pressure are finding ways to secure supplies and reduce losses.

euronews.title: What to know about Mistral's ML4 as it bets on EU sovereignty in the US-China open-weight AI race
euronews.description: Known as “Le Chonk,” the new frontier AI offering from French company Mistral says it will be the strongest open-weight AI outside China, as it bets that European "sovereignty" can win customers in a race increasingly framed as US versus China.

lemonde.description: Environ 86 000 manifestants ont été recensés dans les cortèges qui se sont élancés depuis le milieu de la matinée en province, selon le ministère de l’intérieur, tandis qu’à Paris les manifestants, qui ont défilé à partir de 14 heures, pourraient être entre 20 000 et 40 000 manifestants. Suivez cette journée de mobilisation avec nos envoyés spéciaux.

lemonde.title: Paramount finalise le rachat de Warner Bros Discovery pour 110 milliards de dollars, créant un nouvel empire du cinéma et de la télévision
lemonde.description: Le nouveau groupe, rebaptisé Skydance, réunit CNN, CBS News, HBO et l’univers Harry Potter, une concentration qui inquiète .

lemonde.title: Peste pulmonaire en Russie : ce que l’on sait des traitements et des modes de transmission de cette maladie qui n’a « pas disparu de la planète »
lemonde.description: La mort d’une employée de l’Institut de lutte contre la peste d’Irkoutsk, en Sibérie, vendredi 2 octobre, a suscité l’inquiétude en dépit des déclarations rassurantes des autorités russes et l’Organisation mondiale de la santé.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen et le RN présentent leur contre-budget, avec « 140 milliards d’euros nets d’économies » en cinq ans
lemonde.description: Cette trajectoire budgétaire « sera confortée par l’adoption d’une règle d’or budgétaire constitutionnelle adoptée par référendum », a précisé la cheffe de file du parti d’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: Mistral AI lance un nouveau modèle d’IA censé « réduire l’écart » avec les meilleurs concurrents chinois
lemonde.description: Accusée de s’être laissé distancer dans la performance des modèles d’intelligence artificielle, la start-up française mise sur Mistral Large 4, disponible à partir de mardi.

lemonde.title: Elargissement : la Commission européenne veut redonner de l’élan à une dynamique qui s’essouffle
lemonde.description: L’exécutif communautaire a mis sur la table, mardi 6 octobre, des propositions pour faciliter l’intégration de l’Ukraine à l’Union européenne.

lemonde.title: Comment la FIFA a contourné son règlement pour favoriser la qualification de la République démocratique du Congo à la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: Selon des documents internes dont « Le Monde » a pris connaissance, l’instance présidée par Gianni Infantino n’a appliqué aucune sanction après l’alignement d’un joueur congolais inéligible lors de plusieurs matchs qualificatifs pour le Mondial, passant outre son propre code de discipline, la jurisprudence et les recommandations de ses juristes.

lemonde.title: Un ancien chef du renseignement extérieur allemand arrêté pour « espionnage constitutif de trahison »
lemonde.description: Selon le parquet fédéral allemand, August Hanning aurait notamment utilisé des contenus classifiés, transmis par l’un de ses anciens collaborateurs, afin de rédiger, dans le cadre de ses activités de consultant privé, une analyse pour un « officier d’un service renseignement étranger ».

lemonde.title: Rima Hassan accusée d’avoir « dégradé une exposition » sur le 7-Octobre au Parlement européen après avoir retiré un drapeau israélien de son support
lemonde.description: En visitant une exposition consacrée au 7-Octobre, lundi, l’eurodéputée LFI a retiré un drapeau israélien de son support, faisant accidentellement tomber celui de l’Union européenne, a expliqué son équipe à l’AFP, soulignant que ce geste s’inscrivait « dans la dénonciation du génocide toujours en cours mené par le gouvernement israélien ».

lemonde.title: Œnotourisme : de la montgolfière à l’escape game, le vignoble français multiplie les « expériences »
lemonde.description: Avec plus 12 millions de touristes et 7 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires, le tourisme du vin connaît un succès qui ne se dément pas. Les domaines rivalisent de créativité pour attirer les clients et répondre à la crise structurelle du secteur viticole.

lemonde.title: Ebola : le Kenya confirme son tout premier mort
lemonde.description: Un Kényan vivant en République démocratique du Congo est mort de la maladie à virus Ebola, lundi 5 octobre, dans un hôpital de Nairobi, a annoncé le ministre de la santé kényan. Il s’agit du premier décès lié à cette maladie jamais recensé dans ce pays d’Afrique de l’Est.

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron ferme la porte à un dialogue sur l’avenir de la Polynésie sous l’égide de l’ONU
lemonde.description: L’adjoint du représentant permanent de la France aux Nations unies, Jay Dharmadhikari, a signifié le refus de la France de voir l’ONU s’immiscer dans le dossier sur l’avenir institutionnel du territoire, avant d’ajouter que le président de la République ouvrirait néanmoins « des consultations avec l’ensemble des parties prenantes ».

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, les scandales n’ont pas contrarié l’ascension politique de Flavio Bolsonaro
lemonde.description: Arrivé en tête au premier tour de la présidentielle brésilienne, dimanche 4 octobre, avec 47 % des voix, le fils aîné de l’ex-président Jair Bolsonaro fait l’objet d’une enquête de police pour blanchiment d’argent et corruption.

lemonde.title: A Lens, la quête d’économies au sein d’ateliers consacrés au pouvoir d’achat : « On s’en sort quand même, mais tout est calculé »
lemonde.description: Dans cette ville du Pas-de-Calais, le centre social Vachala, géré par la municipalité socialiste, organise des ateliers prodiguant des conseils sur la gestion d’un budget rogné par la crise énergétique et les coûts des produits alimentaires.

lemonde.title: L’Espagne lève le mandat d’arrêt visant le leader indépendantiste catalan Carles Puigdemont
lemonde.description: Près de neuf ans après son départ vers la Belgique, qui a suivi la tentative de sécession de la Catalogne, M. Puigdemont peut désormais retourner en Espagne.

lemonde.title: Soupçons de peste en Russie : les autorités nient la mise en place de mesures sanitaires, après la mort d’une laborantine
lemonde.description: L’agence de santé publique russe a dénoncé « une fausse information » selon laquelle « un régime sanitaire et épidémiologique renforcé et de restrictions strictes » aurait été instauré dans la région d’Irkoutsk à la suite de la mort d’une technicienne de l’Institut de lutte contre la peste.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : un mois avant les élections de mi-mandat, le spectre d'une crise de régime inédite
france24fr.description: Dans exactement quatre semaines, des millions d'Américains seront convoqués aux urnes. Le 3 novembre, les États-Unis rééliront les 435 membres de la Chambre des représentants et un tiers des 100 sièges du Sénat. À l'approche du scrutin, le monde politique américain est entré en fibrillation. Analyse d’Anne Corpet, chroniqueuse internationale France 24.

france24fr.title: France : Parcoursup dans le viseur des lycéens pour ses critères de sélection flous
france24fr.description: Dans le viseur de beaucoup de lycéens dans la mobilisation en France : la plateforme d’orientation pour les études supérieures Parcoursup. Source d’une grande anxiété pour beaucoup d'élèves, elle est notamment critiquée pour ses critères de sélection flous. Si Sébastien Lecornu a demandé à ses ministres des améliorations pour 2027, les organisations lycéennes réclament de leur côté sa suppression.

france24fr.title: REPLAY : Sébastien Lecornu s'exprime à l'Assemblée nationale sur la mobilisation lycéenne
france24fr.description: Sébastien Lecornu s'est exprimé devant l'Assemblée nationale ce mardi, journée de manifestations inédite après des jours de mobilisation lycéenne. Il a annoncé une suspension des cours en fin de semaine pour "un temps de démocratie interne".

france24fr.title: Saddam Alaya, le Jordanien qui marche pour la paix est arrivé au Rwanda
france24fr.description: 🇷🇼 Le Jordanien Saddam Alaya engagé dans une marche de 23 000 km pour promouvoir la paix et l’éducation est arrivé au Rwanda. Fondateur de l'ONG Hike With Me, il ambitionne de traverser 18 pays et 3 continents, de l’Afrique du Sud à la Russie.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Sébastien Lecornu réfute toute "répression policière" et suspend les cours
Hip-hop : "La Place" fête dix ans de rap, de combats et de nouvelles voix
france24fr.description: Dix ans que La Place fait vibrer Paris au rythme du hip-hop. Sous la Canopée des Halles, cet établissement s’est imposé comme l’un des hauts lieux du hip-hop de la capitale, à la croisée du rap, de la danse, des arts visuels et du débat. Pour célébrer cet anniversaire, plus de cinquante artistes se succèdent pendant dix jours de festival. À cette occasion, Nina Masson reçoit Julien Cholewa, directeur et programmateur de La Place, et Vicky R, rappeuse, compositrice et productrice gabonaise.

france24fr.title: Ebola : le Kenya annonce le premier mort lié au virus jamais recensé sur son sol
france24fr.description: Un Kényan vivant en RD Congo est mort d'Ebola, lundi dans un hôpital de Nairobi, ont annoncé mardi les autorités kényanes. Selon le ministre kényan de la Santé Aden Duale, la victime était tombée malade il y a environ un mois et avait été soignée dans plusieurs hôpitaux, avant de traverser la frontière avec l'Ouganda par la route, puis de prendre un avion pour Nairobi.

france24fr.title: Lycées : une colère légitime ? Parlons-en avec F. Truong, M. Mesnil et V. Gas
france24fr.description: Aujourd'hui, dans "Parlons-en", place à l'analyse des revendications du mouvement lycéen, qui a gagné une partie des établissements en France en trois semaines. La mobilisation a pris de court un gouvernement qui était, semble-t-il, attentif à d'autres colères. Celle des lycéens est-elle justifiée ? S'agit-il d'un problème d'argent, de considération, de société ? Où mènent ces accusations de récupération politique ? Le maintien de l'ordre est-il adapté à des manifestants mineurs ?

france24fr.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : 150 000 manifestants attendus en France avec le soutien des syndicats
france24fr.description: Les lycéens et les étudiants français accentuent la pression sur ​le gouvernement lors d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation. Ce mardi marque 'l'acte III" d'un mouvement de contestation émaillé de nombreuses violences qui gagne tout le pays ​avec le renfort de syndicats et de l'opposition de gauche. Précisions de David Gilberg.

france24fr.title: 1229, 1443, 1973... Retour en images sur les mouvement de contestation étudiants en France
france24fr.description: Aujourd’hui les lycéens français sont dans la rue pour réclamer plus de moyens pour l’éducation. Mais la contestation de la jeunesse remonte à bien plus loin que ce que l’on pourrait croire… Certains historiens considèrent que la première révolte étudiante de l’histoire date de 1229. Historique en images avec Karim Yahiaoui.

france24fr.title: Brésil: Bolsonaro vire en tête
france24fr.description: Flavio Bolsonaro déjoue les pronostics. Il vire en tête du 1er tour de l'élection présidentielle face à Lula. Nouveau virage à (l'extreme-) droite pour le Brésil ? On va plus loin avec Niagalé Bagayoko, Antoine Mariotti et Fanny Lothaire à Rio de Janeiro.

france24fr.title: "Nous avons été naïfs à l'égard du Hamas", affirme l'ex-otage israélienne Shoshan Haran
france24fr.description: Dans un entretien accordé à France 24, l'ex-otage israélienne Shoshan Haran a estimé que ses compatriotes et elle avaient été "naïfs" au sujet du Hamas avant les attaques du 7 octobre 2023 visant notamment son kibboutz. Retenue en otage pendant cinquante jours, elle se rappelle, trois ans après, avoir voulu ne "montrer aucun signe de faiblesse" à ses ravisseurs.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Fifa a-t-elle favorisé la qualification de la RD Congo ?
france24fr.description: Selon une enquête du Monde, la Fifa aurait ignoré une recommandation de ses juristes et son propre code de discipline en ne sanctionnant pas la RD Congo, après l'alignement d'un joueur inéligible lors des barrages africains puis intercontinentaux pour le Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : le rôle clé des réseaux sociaux, dopés à l'intelligence artificielle
france24fr.description: Un des facteurs clés dans la mobilisation lycéenne ces dernières heures, selon les services de renseignements : les réseaux sociaux, dopés à l'intelligence artificielle. Certains maires ont même demandé à ce que ces réseaux sociaux soient temporairement bloqués aux mineurs.

france24fr.title: Projet d'attaque de Fairford : un Britannique de 22 ans arrêté, soupçonné de préparer des actes terroristes
Non, l’armée française n’a pas envoyé des chars contre les blocus de lycéens
france24fr.description: Des internautes accusent l’armée française d’avoir déployé des blindés pour réprimer ces derniers jours les manifestations des lycéens qui demandent l'amélioration de leurs conditions de scolarité. Mais les vidéos censées apporter les preuves de leur déploiement sont trompeuses.

france24fr.title: Projet d'attaque de Fairford : un Britannique de 22 ans arrêté
france24fr.description: La police antiterroriste britannique a annoncé, mardi, l’arrestation d'un Britannique de 22 ans dans le cadre de l’enquête sur l’incident survenu près de la base militaire de Fairford. Il est soupçonné de "préparation d'un acte terroriste".

france24fr.title: Sénégal : plusieurs familles sinistrées après de fortes pluies à Dakar
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, les fortes pluies qui ont frappé le pays dimanche ont fait plusieurs morts et d’importants dégâts. À Dakar, plusieurs familles sont touchées. Le gouvernement dit avoir activé un plan d’urgence d'assistance aux sinistrés.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Zürcher Steuerzahler haben schon wieder mehr Geld bezahlt, als der Kanton für seine Aufgaben benötigt – jetzt braucht es endlich Steuersenkungen
nzz.description: Zürich muss sich im Standortwettbewerb verbessern. Gerade bei der Besteuerung von Unternehmen ist das dringend notwendig.

nzz.title: Ein Antiquar und ein Kunsthändler drehen Kunden angebliche Originale von Picasso und Warhol zum Schnäppchenpreis an
nzz.description: Für die Reproduktionen fertigten die beiden Männer gefälschte Zertifikate an – und verdienten damit Zehntausende Franken.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Eine tote Person nach Brand in Dachstock in Winterthur entdeckt
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: Trump genehmigt Hinrichtung durch Erschiessen für Fort-Hood-Attentäter
nzz.description: Erst vor wenigen Tagen misslang eine Hinrichtung im US-Gliedstaat Tennessee. Nun bewilligt Präsident Donald Trump eine Militärexekution. Es wäre die erste seit 1961.

nzz.title: Kataloniens Ex-Präsident Puigdemont kann nach Hause zurück – doch ein Held ist er dort längst nicht mehr
nzz.description: Das spanische Verfassungsgericht setzt die Amnestie des ehemaligen Separatistenführers durch. Puigdemont kommt damit mitten in einen Wahlkampf, in dem die Themen ganz andere geworden sind.

nzz.title: Die seltsamen Folgen der grossen Trockenheit: An der Zürcher Goldküste muss eine Hafenmole vor dem Bersten gerettet werden
nzz.description: Die schwimmende Mole in Meilen muss mit einem Kran verschoben werden. Denn unten im Wasser schlummert Gefahr.

nzz.title: Ernie und Bert sei Dank: Der Neutrino-Forscher Francis Halzen erhält den Physiknobelpreis
nzz.description: Halzen erhält den Preis für seine entscheidenden Beiträge zum Neutrino-Observatorium Ice Cube, mit dem sich schnelle Geisterteilchen aus den Tiefen des Alls nachweisen lassen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Huthi greifen Flughäfen in Saudiarabien an +++ USA ziehen nach Vorfall auf Luftwaffenstützpunkt alle Bomber aus Grossbritannien ab
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Neue Schülerproteste in Frankreich, nun auch Demos in Belgien: Droht eine Ausweitung der Ausschreitungen?
nzz.description: Die Lage in Frankreich eskaliert zunehmend. Für Dienstag haben die Gewerkschaften zu einem landesweiten Aktionstag an den Schulen aufgerufen. Antworten auf die drängendsten Fragen.

nzz.title: Nach Drohnenangriffen im Schwarzen Meer sinkt ein Handelsschiff
nzz.description: Bulgarien und die EU sind alarmiert: Nach nächtlichen Drohnenangriffen auf Handelsschiffe wächst die Angst vor einer Ausweitung des Krieges. Was bedeutet das für Seefahrer?

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «In diesem Land will kaum noch jemand Lehrer werden»
nzz.description: Frankreichs Bildungskrise hat viele Ursachen – und manche der geforderten Lösungen brauchen Jahre. Der Geschichtslehrer Iannis Roder erklärt, warum die Schüler ungeduldig sind und wo die Politik an ihre Grenzen stösst.

nzz.title: Zehn Monate nach ihrem Horrorsturz weiss Michelle Gisin nicht, ob sie nochmals in den Ski-Weltcup zurückkehrt
nzz.description: Die 32-jährige Engelbergerin will im Oktober erstmals wieder auf den Ski stehen und dann weiterschauen. Sie beschäftigt, dass sie noch immer Fragen zum Unfall hat. Swiss Ski hat den Sturz analysiert.

nzz.title: Saudiarabien hat die Geduld mit den Huthi verloren – Riad zwingt die jemenitischen Islamisten zum Rückzug
nzz.description: Mit saudischer Luftunterstützung haben Truppen der international anerkannten Regierung Jemens die Huthi von der Meerenge Bab al-Mandab vertrieben. Dennoch bleibt ein schneller Sieg über die proiranischen Bergkrieger unwahrscheinlich.

nzz.title: Unbekannte hacken sich ins zentrale Personenregister Dänemarks und verschaffen sich Zugang zu persönlichen Daten von 8,8 Millionen Menschen
nzz.description: Zehn Tage lang konnten die Hacker ungehindert in den persönlichen Daten von lebenden und verstorbenen Däninnen und Dänen stöbern. Die Behörden stehen in der Kritik.

nzz.title: VIDEO - FBI-Festnahme: Wie eine Immobilienmaklerin zur mutmasslichen Agentin Chinas wurde
nzz.description: Eine Immobilienmaklerin aus Kalifornien soll im Auftrag Chinas Angehörige des taiwanischen Präsidenten ausspioniert haben. Anhand von FBI-Akten und Überwachungsbildern rekonstruieren wir die mutmassliche Operation.

nzz.title: Amelia Earhart verschwand 1937 spurlos über dem Pazifik. Endete sie als Schiffbrüchige auf einer winzigen Insel?
nzz.description: Eine neue Forschungsexpedition bricht auf, um das Flugzeugwrack der berühmten Pilotin zu finden.

zeit.title: Landtag Sachsen-Anhalt: AfD-Politiker Hans-Thomas Tillschneider ist Vizelandtagspräsident
zeit.description: Der AfD-Rechtsaußen Hans-Thomas Tillschneider ist vom Landtag in Sachsen-Anhalt zum Vizepräsidenten gewählt worden. Er erhielt fünf Stimmen mehr als die AfD hat.

zeit.title: Pilotprojekt: Neue Methode: Polizei kontrolliert Lkw-Abstand per Drohne
Bundeswehr: Bund will offenbar vier weitere Fregatten bestellen
zeit.description: Die Marine soll wohl vier weitere Kriegsschiffe bekommen. Die Bundesregierung plant laut einem Bericht mit 5,6 Milliarden Euro, bis 2035 sollen die Fregatten fertig sein.

zeit.title: Landtagspräsident in Sachsen-Anhalt: Grüne und Linke sehen in AfD-Landtagspräsident Gefahr für Demokratie
zeit.description: Die Wahl des AfD-Kandidaten Tobias Rausch zum Landtagspräsidenten von Sachsen-Anhalt wird deutlich verurteilt. Grüne und Linke kritisieren auch das BSW und die CDU.

zeit.title: Landtagspräsident in Sachsen-Anhalt: Grüne und Linke sehen in AfD-Landtagspräsident Gefahr für Demokratie
zeit.description: Die Wahl des AfD-Kandidaten Tobias Rausch zum Landtagspräsidenten von Sachsen-Anhalt wird deutlich verurteilt. Grüne und Linke kritisieren auch das BSW und die CDU.

zeit.title: Tennis: Sinner beendet Saison: Zverevs Riesenchance auf Nummer 1
Gelebte Tradition: Ruth Liebscher ist das Dresdner Stollenmädchen 2026
Wohnungsmarkt in Spanien: Spanische Regierung beschließt erneut Mieterschutzdekrete
zeit.description: Das Scheitern eines Mietpakets führte zur Ausrufung von Neuwahlen. Dadurch kann Spaniens Regierung auf eine Mehrheit für ihr Projekt in einer Art Notparlament hoffen.

zeit.title: Kanzlerbesuch: Merz kommt zum CSU-Parteitag nach München
Mehr Stimmen als gedacht: CDU rätselt: Woher kamen die Stimmen für AfD-Präsident?
Messerattacke: 17-Jähriger nach lebensgefährlichem Messerstich in U-Haft
Sportpolitik: IOC verrät: Das sind Münchens Rivalen um Olympia 2036
Landtag: Frei besorgt über Extra-Stimmen für AfD-Landtagspräsidenten
Infraplan 2026: Verkehrsministerium stellt neuen Plan zur Bahn-Sanierung vor
zeit.description: Mit dem Infraplan will die Bundesregierung die Modernisierung des Bahnnetzes besser koordinieren. Gewerkschaften kritisieren, dass die Finanzierung nicht geklärt ist.

zeit.title: Ausstellung im Bucerius Kunst Forum: Schlafende Hunde wecken
zeit.description: Jüdinnen und Juden zählten zu den frühen Förderern moderner Kunst. Dann raubten die Nazis ihre Sammlungen. Eine Ausstellung in Hamburg bringt 15 davon wieder zusammen.

observador.title: Host Douro: o futuro da hospitalidade
observador.description: João Gonçalves, Presidente da CIM Douro, faz o balanço da 2.ª edição do Host Douro, destacando a aposta numa hospitalidade de excelência e num futuro sustentável para a região.

observador.title: "Incidentes russos minam a relação com os países europeus"
observador.description: Nuno Gouveia destaca a pressão cada vez maior por parte da Rússia junto da Europa que pode levar a uma resposta mais dura da UE. Sublinha discurso positivo de Luís Montenegro no Parlamento Europeu.

observador.title: Sobrelotação nas escolas. "Tem tudo para correr mal"
observador.description: Ministério da Educação revelou que pelo menos 459 turmas em todo o país têm 30 alunos ou mais. Ao redor de Lisboa, o excesso de estudantes em escolas pequenas é um problema há muito mais tempo.

observador.title: O homem que parecia não ter salvação
observador.description: A psicóloga Ana Nunes da Silva acompanhou um homem de 70 anos, com um problema de alcoolismo que durava há décadas, e assistiu a uma transformação inesperada que ainda hoje a comove.

observador.title: "A Caça ao Estripador de Lisboa" é agora um teatro imersivo
observador.description: O Podcast Plus transformado num espetáculo dá nova vida à investigação do assassino em série que aterrorizou Lisboa nos anos 90. Estreia-se a 28 de outubro e os bilhetes já estão à venda.

observador.title: Trump ordena morte por fuzilamento a ex-militar
observador.description: O Presidente dos EUA aprovou a execução por um pelotão de fuzilamento de Nidal Hasan, antigo psiquiatra do Exército norte-americano. Hasan matou 13 pessoas na base militar de Fort Hood, no Texas.

observador.title: 15h. Paris. Estudantes protestam por melhor ensino
observador.description: Violentos protestos que começaram nos arredores da capital francesa e acabaram por alastrar a todo o país. Ainda, primeiro ministro espanhol anunciou novas medidas para resolver crise na habitação.

observador.title: Um morto e um ferido grave em incêndio urbano no Montijo
observador.description:
O alerta de incêndio foi dado às 9h16 e o fogo foi considerado extinto às 9h31, tendo sido encaminhados 29 operacionais para o local.
O ferido grave foi transportado para o Hospital do Barreiro.

observador.title: Publicidade fora de casa: estar em todo o lado já não chega
observador.description: A publicidade exterior está a mudar: mais digital e mais próxima dos hábitos de quem circula pela cidade. Vasco Perestrelo, CEO da MOP, explica como chegar às pessoas no momento certo.

observador.title: Negócio fechado: Paramount é agora dona da Warner Bros
observador.description: Após meses de análise regulatória, ficou esta terça-feira concluída a aquisição da Warner Bros Discovery pela Paramount. A empresa que resulta da fusão é a Skydance.

observador.title: Tenista espanhol Carlos Alcaraz regressa aos títulos
observador.description: Carlos Alcaraz conquista o título em Tóquio pelo segundo ano seguido, após vencer contra o Jiri Lehecka. Alcaraz teve uma lesão no pulso, que o impediu de participar em Roland Garros e Wimbledon.

observador.title: Cinco acusados por rixa que levou à morte de jovem
observador.description: Rixa aconteceu em 2024 e provocou a morte de um rapaz de 16 anos, por esfaqueamento. Dois menores envolvidos na luta foram julgados pelo Tribunal do Porto em fevereiro de 2025.

observador.title: Congresso: UGT sem nome "consensual" para a presidência
observador.description: Tendência social-democrata dentro da UGT apresentou nome de Francisco Pimentel para a presidência da central. Deputado não reúne consenso e em vésperas do congresso Mourão admite candidato socialista.

observador.title: Paulo Branco é homenageado na Mostra de Cinema de São Paulo
observador.description: Prémio Leon Cakoff, segundo a organização, visa "homenagear personalidades do cinema que há décadas se dedicam a construir as suas carreiras de maneiras originais, criativas e marcantes".

observador.title: Puigdemont pode regressar a Espanha sem ser detido
observador.description: Juiz do Supremo espanhol suspendeu as ordens de detenção emitidas em 2017 contra Puigdemont, Comín e Lluís Puig após o Constitucional determinar que a lei da amnistia se aplica ao crime de corrupção.

observador.title: Defesa. Movimento defende Serviço Nacional de Cidadania
observador.description: Plataforma defende o fim do Dia da Defesa Nacional e avança com a necessidade de criar um Serviço Nacional de Cidadania universal e obrigatório, com uma duração de referência entre seis e doze meses.

observador.title: "Não basta reformar, também é preciso investir na Justiça"
observador.description: Rafael Vale Reis e Pedro Marinho Falcão elogiam várias medidas da reforma da Justiça Administrativa e Fiscal proposta pelo Governo mas alertam: são necessários mais juízes e oficiais de justiça.

observador.title: PS quis fechar rápido OE. Mas ainda tem "atoleiro" a evitar
observador.description: Carneiro quis evitar uma novela e deu sinal de viabilização mesmo sem conhecer o documento — contrariando o que sempre disse. No partido, o alívio convive com avisos sobre a batalha na especialidade.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Sorge vor Eskalation bei Schülerprotesten gegen Missstände
spiegel.description: Marode Schulen, volle Klassen, fehlende Lehrer: Frankreichs Schüler protestieren seit Tagen, manche liefern sich Ausschreitungen mit der Polizei. Die Sorge vor einer weiteren Eskalation wächst.

spiegel.title: Bully Herbig verlässt »LOL«, Carolin Kebekus übernimmt
spiegel.description: Sieben Staffeln moderierte er »LOL: Last One Laughing« bei Amazon Prime, nun übergibt Bully Herbig den Job an Carolin Kebekus. Er hat bereits eine andere Show.

spiegel.title: RAF Fairford: Weiterer Verdächtiger festgenommen
spiegel.description: Die Zahl der Festgenommenen im Fall Fairford steigt weiter: Die britische Polizei hat einen 22-Jährigen festgenommen. Er soll eine terroristische Handlung vorbereitet haben.

spiegel.title: Amokläufer von Fort Hood: Donald Trump genehmigt erste Militärhinrichtung seit 65 Jahren – per Erschießung
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat die Hinrichtung von Amokläufer Nidal Hasan genehmigt. Wie üblich sind Todesurteile für Mitglieder der US-Armee? Wie fehlerhaft sind Exekutionen und warum kann der US-Präsident eine Hinrichtung anordnen? Die Antworten.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Rechtsextremer AfD-Mann wird Landtagspräsident
spiegel.description: Ein Rechtsextremist steht an der Spitze eines deutschen Landtags: AfD-Mann Tobias Rausch ist neuer Parlamentspräsident in Sachsen-Anhalt. Was bedeutet das? Und wie geht es jetzt weiter? Einordnungen von SPIEGEL-Korrespondent Peter Maxwill.

spiegel.title: Krebs am Arbeitsplatz: EU will Grenzwerte für gesundheitsschädliche Stoffe verschärfen
spiegel.description: Krebs ist die häufigste Ursache für arbeitsbedingte Todesfälle in der EU. Nun greift das Parlament durch. Neue Grenzwerte für verschiedene krebserregende Schadstoffe sollen demnach mehr als 20.000 Erkrankungen verhindern.

spiegel.title: Russland: Was über den Pestverdacht nach dem Tod einer Frau in Sibirien bekannt ist
spiegel.description: In Sibirien ist eine Frau an einer »Lungenentzündung unbekannter Herkunft« gestorben. War Lungenpest die Ursache? Offizielle wiegeln ab. Doch die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen sind auffällig.

spiegel.title: Hollywood: Paramount finalisiert Warner-Übernahme
spiegel.description: Dutzenden Milliarden Dollar an Schulden und Sorgen um die redaktionelle Unabhängigkeit zum Trotz: Die Fusion der Medienkonzerne Paramount und Warner Brothers ist abgeschlossen. Das neue Unternehmen heißt Skydance.

spiegel.title: Tesla Grünheide: Abgelehnter Bewerber droht mit Anschlägen und schickt Schweineaugen
spiegel.description: Nach einer Absage von Tesla hat ein Bewerber mit Anschlägen gedroht, verschickte zudem verwesende Schweineaugen. Gegen eine Geldstrafe von 13.000 Euro legt er dann Einspruch ein – und fehlt bei der anschließenden Verhandlung.

spiegel.title: Günstig kochen: Rezept für cremige Zaddy-Bohnen
spiegel.description: Wir nehmen uns ein Vorbild an einem der elegantesten Männer Hollywoods, um dann alles über den Haufen zu werfen und den Zorn Italiens auf uns zu ziehen – für ein langes Leben und den schmalen Geldbeutel.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Kanzleramt gab Alleinerziehenden Tipps gegen »Selbstmitleid« – Broschüre nun offline
spiegel.description: »Denken Sie nicht, alle Probleme wären gelöst, wenn Sie mehr Geld hätten«: Fragwürdige Ratschläge an Alleinerziehende haben im Netz für Aufregung gesorgt. Österreichs Familienministerium räumt Fehler ein.

spiegel.title: Nicht-invasiver Pränataltest: Abgeordnete von Union, SPD, Grünen und Linken streiten über Kassenleistung
spiegel.description: Welche Auswirkungen hat der nicht invasive Pränataltest? Abgeordnete von Union, SPD, Grünen und Linken streiten, ob Schwangere den Test zu oft machen und die Krankenkasse ihn nicht mehr bezahlen soll.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Jugendliche sticht an Schule in Istanbul mit Messer um sich - acht Verletzte
spiegel.description: Erneut ist es an einer Schule in der Türkei zu einer Gewalttat gekommen. Eine 15-Jährige hat Kinder mit einem Messer attackiert – offenbar wahllos.

phys-org.title: Heavy fermions emerge at an atomic-layer interface, unlocking new ways to design quantum materials
phys-org.description: A research team led by the University of Osaka has directly observed, for the first time, an unusual heavy-fermion state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. Such states are closely linked to exotic quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, and the finding opens new possibilities for designing quantum materials through their interfaces.

phys-org.title: Popular TikTok docs have big influence on Gen Z followers, new research finds
phys-org.description: Young adults following physicians on TikTok consider them more accessible, credible and altruistic than their own doctors, even when the physician-influencers are selling products. Moreover, the followers haven't actually confirmed the influencers' medical credentials. Those are the main findings of a new study from Virginia Commonwealth University, co-authored by Suzanne Makarem, Ph.D., and published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs.

phys-org.title: Where are the best places for life in the cosmos? A universe in a supercomputer yields an answer
phys-org.description: Earth seems like a troubled place right now, but at least our cosmic surroundings appear peaceful. This is not universally true, as explosions, collisions and other dangers lurk in other places and times.

phys-org.title: To keep GPS constellations from drifting, look to the moon
phys-org.description: Global positioning systems are a key feature in everyday life for much of the world's population. Whether it's ensuring a ship delivers its goods safely or helping you avoid a road closure on your commute home, GPS can help.

phys-org.title: Warming oceans reshape plankton, potentially leaving fish with less nutritious food
phys-org.description: The world is changing. As humans, we tend to focus on what happens on land, but the planet's food systems depend on both terrestrial and marine ecosystems.

phys-org.title: A symbiotic marketplace: Gutless worms swap essential bacterial partners over time
phys-org.description: A typical scene at a local farmers market: Various stalls offer fruit, vegetables and much more. Every customer has their favorite stalls, though these may change occasionally. Some symbiotic relationships seem to work just like that, a study by researchers from the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology reveals in Science Advances.

phys-org.title: How political, cultural, and economic forces can shape the risk of zoonotic disease
phys-org.description: In eastern Ethiopia, pressures like conflict and displacement are changing how people and their camels travel, shifting livestock into new environments and potentially influencing the risk of zoonotic diseases spreading between animals and humans.

phys-org.title: Can a passing black hole disturbance leave a trace in Hawking radiation?
phys-org.description: Black holes, despite their extreme nature, are described by surprisingly few basic parameters: their mass, charge and spin. Two black holes may have formed for completely different reasons and passed through very different histories, yet still end up in the same final state. John Wheeler summarized this idea with the famous phrase "black holes have no hair."

phys-org.title: Bacteria use collisions to navigate crowded environments, micro-maze experiments reveal
phys-org.description: Some bacteria can sense when they bump into each other and use these interactions to shape how the group organizes and moves. This discovery reveals a new way microbes explore their environments using physical feedback rather than chemical signals.

phys-org.title: AI chatbots may increase accurate political knowledge
phys-org.description: As voters seeking information about political issues increasingly turn to LLMs to do research, will AI lead them astray with hallucinations and bias, distorting the democratic process? Maybe not, according to a study of AI use in the 2024 U.K. election, published in PNAS Nexus.

phys-org.title: Molecular complexity as a signature of life
phys-org.description: An abundance of complex molecules has been proposed as a universal signature of life.

phys-org.title: Vanillin provides a sweet solution for chronic wound healing
phys-org.description: A team from Flinders University's Biomedical Nanoengineering Laboratory has found that vanillin has pronounced antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, making it a good candidate for wound-healing formulations. Their work is published in the International Journal of Pharmaceutics.

phys-org.title: Blue light could cut food poisoning from raw chicken
phys-org.description: A low-power blue light could be the key to significantly reducing food poisoning caused by raw chicken in the U.K., scientists at the University of Reading have found. Campylobacter is the most common cause of bacterial food poisoning worldwide. In the U.K. alone, there are hundreds of thousands of cases each year, costing an estimated £700 million annually in health care and lost productivity.

phys-org.title: Counting purpose and connection could reveal overlooked benefits of bike paths and parks
phys-org.description: It's often the sight of heavy digging machinery that makes us question how our taxes and property taxes are being spent. As a new project begins, we may wonder why money is being spent on that and not on other things.

phys-org.title: New report exposes modern poverty and inequality in one of Britain's 'most affluent cities'
phys-org.description: The University of York's Cost of Living Research Group has examined modern living standards across the city and revealed the extent of hidden pockets of poverty and inequality in one of the North's most affluent cities.

phys-org.title: Africa's rhinos often get the spotlight—but Indonesia's two rhino species are far closer to extinction
phys-org.description: Small, hairy and cheekily charismatic. Those words sprang to mind when I first met a Sumatran rhinoceros (Dicerorhinus sumatrensis) after traversing the maze of wooden slat paths at the conservation center in the dense, humid forests of Malaysian Borneo.

phys-org.title: As the planet warms, cities like Bangkok could be increasingly inundated by deadly floods
phys-org.description: In the humid tropics of Southeast Asia, afternoon thunderstorms roll through almost every day. Daytime heat causes towering, fluffy cumulonimbus clouds to form and swell before unleashing torrential rain on cities such as Singapore, Hong Kong and Bangkok. In these places, drainage systems are designed to cope with short, heavy downpours.

phys-org.title: Yosemite's meadows can be restored, but it will take time and effort
phys-org.description: Researchers at Colorado State University are leading an attempt to restore Yosemite National Park's iconic meadows before it's too late by reintroducing native plants that once covered the landscape. Results are published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences.

undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: Sino-American Stability Without Trust
proj-syn.description: The main outcomes of the Trump-Xi summit—the two-month trade extension, the dialogue on AI, and even the carefully chosen language on Taiwan—point to Sino-American relations being in a holding pattern. For both sides, the main task is to prevent managed rivalry from devolving into outright confrontation.

proj-syn.title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
proj-syn.description: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

proj-syn.title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
proj-syn.description: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia's usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

proj-syn.title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
proj-syn.description: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

proj-syn.title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
proj-syn.description: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

proj-syn.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
proj-syn.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

proj-syn.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
proj-syn.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

proj-syn.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
proj-syn.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

proj-syn.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

proj-syn.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
proj-syn.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

proj-syn.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
proj-syn.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

proj-syn.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
proj-syn.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.
